skill.name: set-up-cloudflare-google-ads-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up profit on ad spend (POAS) bidding in Google Ads for a Cloudflare website without a store plugin. Use Product Metrics to check tracking, estimate order profit, and choose a starting target ROAS based on profit.
skill.summary: Use estimated order profit instead of revenue to guide Google Ads bidding for a Cloudflare website.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are Markdown formatting, routine account checks, or advertising terminology; no evidence of host reconnaissance, prompt injection, or covert exfiltration was found. Confirmed risks include live tool calls, detailed order access, mutable remote instructions, and an unpinned installer. The setup also leaves gaps in permission review, browser link validation, and approval for unrelated data sharing.

remediation.issue: Live tool execution and access to detailed order records
remediation.suggestion: Verify the CLI and MCP endpoints, confirm the workspace and property before writes, and use only the test order fields needed to verify tracking.

remediation.issue: Unpinned installer and mutable documentation fallback
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer package version and skill source revision. Bundle reviewed references and treat fetched documentation as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Cloudflare approval guidance does not explain permission scope
remediation.suggestion: List each required permission and why it is needed. Ask the administrator to verify the account and zone, and stop if the grant differs.

remediation.issue: The POAS setup can enable data sharing beyond the requested purpose
remediation.suggestion: List the data and destinations before setup. Require separate approval for unrelated signals, extra ad channels, or Enhanced Conversions.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs lack an explicit destination check
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS destinations and redirect origins against an approved list before presenting sign-in or authorization links.

semantic_findings.title: Blanket Cloudflare Permission Approval
semantic_findings.description: Troubleshooting tells the administrator to "approve every permission" without listing the expected grants. The integration adds tracking to every page in the selected domain.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The blanket approval and site-wide deployment are explicit. No evidence establishes the exact permission scope or shows that any unnecessary permission was granted.

semantic_findings.title: Setup Extends Beyond Profit Conversion Data
semantic_findings.description: The profit guide directs creation of eight conversion actions, including signals unrelated to profit bidding. Connection guides also direct users toward additional ad channels and Enhanced Conversions without a separate POAS scope check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Google Ads receives the additional signals even when their actions are secondary. The guides describe consent controls, but do not separate these choices from the requested setup.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Handoff Does Not Verify Destination
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the user to open a URL from a tool response without checking the destination. A compromised response could send the user to an unexpected sign-in or permission prompt.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff instructions show no origin check before a user opens the URL. No evidence shows that a malicious link was served.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money after product costs and fees. Use Product Metrics to verify Cloudflare purchase tracking and prepare Google Ads to bid on estimated profit.
actual_capabilities: Check which setup steps are complete in an authorized Product Metrics workspace through its CLI or MCP server.
Guide the user through connecting the Cloudflare storefront and Google Ads client account, including required Merchant Center access.
Explain how to set a product cost percentage and account for shipping, handling, returns, and payment fees.
Use a test order to check whether both revenue and estimated profit appear.
Compare profit and revenue conversion actions, then verify which action is primary after the user updates Google Ads.
Suggest a starting target ROAS using the campaign's current POAS, when available.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a storefront proxied through Cloudflare, and the correct Google Ads client account linked to Merchant Center.
Cloudflare website orders do not provide actual product costs. Profit is estimated and is not sent for orders with unknown costs.
The user must authorize connections and change conversion goals and bidding settings in Google Ads.
This workflow does not cover new customer, returning customer, or lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Check whether profit bidding is ready
use_cases.description: Review Cloudflare tracking, consent, and cost settings before using profit as a conversion value.

use_cases.title: Plan a switch for one campaign
use_cases.description: Use current campaign POAS to suggest a starting target and identify which conversion action should steer bidding.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing profit values
use_cases.description: Trace a test purchase from the order confirmation page and check whether missing costs explain a revenue-only result.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm what needs to be in place.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what my Cloudflare storefront needs before I can bid on profit in Google Ads. List the prerequisites without making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review tracking status
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: check an existing Product Metrics setup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for the Product Metrics property I confirm. List what is complete and what needs my approval. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a missing profit value
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: revenue appears for a test order but profit does not.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check why my test order shows revenue but no profit. Check consent and cost settings, and omit customer and order identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a single-campaign switch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: move an existing campaign from revenue to profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my approved campaign's current POAS to suggest a starting target ROAS. Explain how I can change the conversion goal and verify the result. Do not change campaign settings.

output_examples.input: My test purchase shows revenue but no profit. What should I check?
output: In Profit tracking, check that the product cost percentage and additional costs are active.
Confirm that the test purchase had analytics and ad user data consent.
Run another test purchase and check for both values before changing the campaign goal.

output_examples.input: My campaign has a current POAS of 1.5. What starting target should I consider?
output: Consider a starting target ROAS of 150% when the campaign uses the Profit conversion action.
Start with one campaign. Keep its old purchase action secondary so only one purchase action guides bidding.
Review results after a few weeks before adjusting the target.

best_practices: Confirm the Cloudflare zone, Product Metrics property, Google Ads client account, and required permissions before authorizing any connection.
Use a consented test order to verify revenue and estimated profit before making any conversion action primary.
Start with one campaign and derive the initial target from that campaign's measured POAS.
anti_patterns: Copying a revenue-based ROAS target directly to a profit-based conversion.
Leaving profit and an existing purchase action primary for the same campaign goal.
Enabling extra ad destinations or sharing customer data without separate approval.

faq.question: How is POAS different from ROAS?
faq.answer: POAS compares profit with ad spend. Revenue-based ROAS compares revenue with ad spend.

faq.question: Can I use Cloudflare Tracking without a store plugin?
faq.answer: Yes. Your storefront must use a proxied Cloudflare DNS record, and an authorized administrator must approve the connection.

faq.question: What if my website does not report product costs?
faq.answer: Set a fallback percentage for product costs and add other costs. The resulting profit is an estimate.

faq.question: What happens to orders with missing costs or a loss?
faq.answer: An order with unknown costs is sent with revenue only. An order sold at a loss has a profit conversion value of zero.

faq.question: Who changes the bidding goal in Google Ads?
faq.answer: You change the goal in Google Ads. The skill can read back the conversion action status after you finish.

faq.question: Do I need Merchant Center and a paid plan?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow requires Product Metrics Pro and Merchant Center connected to the Google Ads client account.
